explicit_evidence_changes.baseline: During an ICE hiring surge, an AI-assisted résumé-screening process reportedly classified some inexperienced applicants as having law-enforcement experience and routed them into shortened training. ICE manually reviewed affected cases and directed additional training; the reviewed reporting did not identify uncorrected field deployment or resulting public-safety harm.
explicit_evidence_changes.candidate: During an ICE hiring surge, AI-assisted résumé screening reportedly assigned law-enforcement experience to inexperienced applicants and routed them into shortened training. Reports described later manual review and additional training. Assignment to field offices does not itself establish enforcement work. In January 2026 DHS acknowledged a technological error, said 200 of 12,000 hires were affected and reported that they had gone to FLETC for full training. DHS denied enforcement duties without appropriate training and credentials. The reviewed evidence does not independently resolve every recruit’s training or duty history, or establish resulting public-safety harm.

baseline.factual_basis: NBC News reported, based on agency and source accounts, that résumé-screening output assigned law-enforcement experience to some applicants who lacked it. ICE manually reviewed the affected cases and directed additional training. The reviewed evidence does not establish that the recruits performed field duties without correction or caused public-safety harm.
baseline.governance_interpretation: Reported screening errors changed training-path decisions. Manual review and added training are supported corrections. Validation records and the information supplied for applicant challenges remain unresolved. Uncorrected field deployment and public-safety harm are not established.
baseline.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows why automated screening in high-consequence hiring must separate inferential signals from verified qualifications before those signals control training or deployment pathways.
assessment_boundaries: The principal independent report relies partly on unnamed sources and does not disclose the model, decision rule or complete number of affected recruits.
No reviewed evidence establishes downstream field harm or discriminatory allocation across protected groups.

candidate.factual_basis: The preserved NBC report attributes mistaken experience designations, shortened training assignments and subsequent correction to source accounts. The complete NBC article remains inaccessible in this review environment. UNILAD’s January 16 article supplies a directly obtained DHS response: the agency describes a corrected technological problem affecting 200 of 12,000 hires, says final hirings were unaffected, and says the affected recruits completed onboarding and reported to FLETC for full law-enforcement training. Reporting to training is not proof of completion. DHS denies enforcement work without appropriate training and credentials. Assignment to a field office is a distinct proposition from performing arrests. No inspected personnel, training or duty records independently settle the disputed field-use question. The anonymous Reddit testimony and unrelated fatal shooting described around the UNILAD statement are excluded from this occurrence’s causal basis.
candidate.governance_interpretation: The reported experience designation acquired consequential force through training-path assignment. Manual review and added training are corrective responses. The agency’s denial of unqualified enforcement work bounds the claim but does not independently prove all corrections preceded every duty assignment. Screening validation, applicant challenge information and the full personnel chronology remain unknown. No public-safety consequence is attributed to the screening error on the inspected evidence.
candidate.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows why automated screening in high-consequence hiring must separate inferential signals from verified qualifications before those signals control training or deployment pathways.
assessment_boundaries: The originating NBC article remains indirectly reviewed; source attribution and access limitations are preserved.
DHS supplied a count and denial of unqualified enforcement work. These claims are not independently checked against personnel or duty records.
Field-office assignment, enforcement work, reporting for full training and completing that training are separate facts.
Unrelated shootings, general hiring criticism and anonymous Reddit testimony do not establish this error’s consequences.
